hints: Take logarithms of both sides of \(2^y=3^{1-2x}\) so that the exponents become coefficients.
Expand \((1-2x)\ln3\) and divide by \(\ln2\) to express \(y\) in the form \(mx+c\).
Identify the exact coefficient of \(x\) as the gradient; do not replace the logarithms by decimals.
walkthrough:
Take the natural logarithm (or logarithm to any base) of both sides:
$$\ln(2^y) = \ln(3^{1 - 2x})$$

Apply the power law of logarithms $\ln(u^k) = k\ln u$:
$$y\ln 2 = (1 - 2x)\ln 3$$
Observe that this equation is of the standard linear form $y = mx + c$, where $m$ and $c$ are constants. Hence, the graph of $y$ against $x$ is a straight line.

State the exact gradient $m$ of the line:
$$\text{Gradient} = -\dfrac{2\ln 3}{\ln 2} \quad \left(\text{or } -\dfrac{\ln 9}{\ln 2} = -\log_2 9\right)$$

hints: At the intersection, substitute \(y=3x\) into the logarithmic straight-line equation found in part (a).
Collect the terms containing \(x\) to obtain \(x(3\ln2+2\ln3)=\ln3\).
Use logarithm laws to combine the denominator into the logarithm of a single integer before giving the required form.
walkthrough:
Substitute the equation of the intersecting line $y = 3x$ into the equation $y\ln 2 = \ln 3 - 2x\ln 3$:
$$(3x)\ln 2 = \ln 3 - 2x\ln 3$$

Group all terms containing $x$ on the left-hand side:
$$3x\ln 2 + 2x\ln 3 = \ln 3$$
$$x(3\ln 2 + 2\ln 3) = \ln 3$$

Apply the power law of logarithms to simplify each term inside the bracket:
$$3\ln 2 = \ln(2^3) = \ln 8$$
$$2\ln 3 = \ln(3^2) = \ln 9$$

Apply the product law of logarithms $\ln u + \ln v = \ln(uv)$:
$$3\ln 2 + 2\ln 3 = \ln 8 + \ln 9 = \ln(8 \times 9) = \ln 72$$

Substitute this back into the equation for $x$:
$$x\ln 72 = \ln 3$$
Confirm the required format $\dfrac{\ln a}{\ln b}$ with integers $a = 3$ and $b = 72$.
